prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
Do you need a residential or commercial tester/repairer? I can look up specific companies near you if you want — tell me whether this is for a home or business and confirm your zip code (Liberty has a few).

Meanwhile, here’s how to find a qualified backflow tester/repairer near Liberty, MO and what to ask:

How to find one
- Check with the City of Liberty Utilities or Public Works — many cities keep a list of approved/certified testers and will tell you testing/reporting requirements.
- Search Google Maps/Yelp/Angi/HomeAdvisor for “backflow tester,” “backflow prevention testing,” or “cross connection testing” in Liberty, MO (zip 64068).
- Look for local plumbing and irrigation companies that advertise “backflow testing” or “RPZ testing.”

What to look for / questions to ask
- Certification: Ask if the technician is a certified backflow prevention assembly tester (ask for certificate or tester ID). Municipalities sometimes require specific state or local certification.
- Experience: Ask how many years/assemblies they test per year and whether they’ve worked with local utilities.
- Reporting: Confirm they will supply a completed test report and submit it to the city/water utility if required.
- Parts & repairs: Can they do on-site repairs and supply replacement parts if the device fails? Get an estimate for common repair costs.
- Insurance & licenses: Verify business license and liability insurance.
- Price & timing: Ask cost per assembly (typical range for testing often falls roughly $60–$150 depending on device and region) and when they can come.
- Device info: Tell them the type of device (RPZ, DCVA, PVB, pressure vacuum breaker), serial number and location (irrigation, commercial process, boiler feed, etc.).

What to have ready when they arrive
- Location of assembly, gate or access instructions, model/serial if visible, last test date, any compliance letters from the city.
